key_insight: Temperature-dependent Raman and XRD separate two distinct structural events in SrLaCoNbO6: a low-temperature isostructural octahedral distortion near 300 °C and a higher-temperature symmetry-breaking transition near 750 °C.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical lab-scale workflow to diagnose functional structure changes in ordered double perovskites, helping guide thermal stability, phase-control, and defect-structure design.
method: Combined Raman spectroscopy and laboratory XRD from 25–900 °C
Tracked phonon frequency/linewidth renormalization and XRD peak evolution
Quantified octahedral distortion parameters and used group-theoretical/Rietveld analysis
evidence_signal: Two anomalies were observed at T_OD = 300±25 °C and T_PT = 750±25 °C, supported by phonon renormalization, suppression/evolution of characteristic XRD reflections, and refinement-based phase assignment.
watch_item: The transition temperatures are approximate and the structural interpretation depends on careful peak indexing and distortion analysis, so similar signatures in related perovskites may require cross-validation.
paper_title: Disentangling octahedral distortion and symmetry breaking in the ordered double perovskite SrLaCoNbO$_6$
